summary.en-US: Convert videos to 320 kbps MP3 files and share them

description.en-US:
An app that does one thing: turn videos into MP3 files.

Pick one or more videos, and each one's audio track is extracted and
re-encoded to a 320 kbps CBR MP3 saved in your Downloads folder. When
it is done you get a list of the files, each with a Share button — so
sending them to a cloud folder, Telegram, WhatsApp or anywhere else
is one tap away.

* 320 kbps constant bitrate, encoded with LAME
* Batch conversion — pick as many videos as you like
* Saved straight to Downloads, visible in your file manager
* Share individual files or all of them at once
* Works with anything your phone can play: MP4, MKV, WebM, 3GP…
* Videos can also be sent to the app from another app's share sheet
* Conversion keeps running when you leave the app

No accounts, no network access, no ads, no tracking. Everything
happens on the device.

Bundles LAME 3.100 (LGPL-2.1-or-later).

summary.en-US: Black-and-white, text-only launcher in the spirit of the Light Phone

description.en-US:
Reader's Launcher turns the home screen into a single column of words. No icons,
no colours, no wallpaper: white on black, or black on white — flip between the two
with a double tap, from the "Reader's theme" quick-settings tile, or in settings.

* Tiles are plain text: an app, or a category that opens a text list of apps.
* A grid of 3 to 5 squares pinned at the bottom holds the unavoidable apps (phone,
  messages…) with their icons rendered as monochrome glyphs.
* Built-in widgets: clock; weather (Open-Meteo, no account, tap for five days);
  agenda (next event, swipe for the following ones); tasks (first task of a
  Tasks.org list, tick to complete, + to add — Tasks.org syncs with CalDAV, Google
  Tasks, Microsoft To Do or keeps lists offline). Standard app widgets can be added too.
* Swipe up for the alphabetical app list with search and the usual long-press
  actions (add to home, category, rename, hide, app info, uninstall).
* Swipe up and hold on the home screen for a text list of recently used apps.
* Swipe down for notifications. Export and import the whole setup as a JSON file.
* Two books beside the home screen: swipe right or left to read (EPUB, MOBI, FB2,
  text), tap to turn pages, position remembered per book. Reading made effortless.
* English by default; French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian when the device
  uses them.

Serif, sans or monospace; three text sizes; left or centred. No ads, no tracking.

summary.en-US: Plays retreat recordings offline, with nothing able to interrupt them

description.en-US:
Retreat Player plays MP3s of dhamma talks, bells, and chanting during a
meditation retreat — built on the same principle as Retreat Timer: once
playback starts, nothing interrupts it.

* Every recording is downloaded into the app's own storage when it is loaded,
  so playback needs no network — airplane mode is fine.
* Playback runs in a foreground service holding a wake lock: the system
  cannot kill or pause it, even with the screen off for an hour-long talk.
* The screen stays on while a recording plays — no lock, no screensaver —
  showing the progress the whole time.
* A recording plays only because you pressed play, and only once: when it
  ends, nothing else starts automatically.

Loading and organising:

* Tap + to load recordings from the phone, from a shared kDrive folder
  (public link — read-only, no password), or from a podcast feed; the link
  and feed URLs are remembered for next time.
* Tiles are filed into two sections — Bells & chanting on top (used every
  day), then Dharma talks — and ordered by hand with arrows.
* The player shows elapsed and remaining time together, with play, pause,
  stop, 10-second jumps, and back-to-beginning.

No ads, no tracking, no accounts.

summary.en-US: Rings one or three meditation bells on schedule, even in deep sleep

description.en-US:
Retreat Timer rings a recording of singing-bowl bells at the times of day you
choose — the signal to begin or end a sitting — so a meditation retreat keeps
running on schedule even when the teacher is not present. Each time can ring
three bells or a single bell, whichever that moment in the day calls for.

Built for one job: the bells ring no matter what.

* Exact alarms via the same mechanism the stock Clock app uses, so they fire on
  time even when the device is locked, asleep, or in Doze for hours.
* A foreground service holds a wake lock and plays through the alarm stream, so
  the system cannot mute or kill the bells mid-ring.
* Alarms are re-armed automatically after a reboot, time change, or app update.
* A readiness light turns green once battery optimisation and notifications are
  set, so the teacher can leave knowing the schedule is safe.

Easy to set up:

* Tap Add bell and pick the time. The picker opens ready for typing, so any
  minute is set directly — 06:47, not just 06:45 — with a dial one tap away.
* In that same picker, choose three bells or one for this time — three to open
  and close a sitting, one for the smaller markers in a day. Preview either
  before setting it. The schedule shows a small x3 or x1 badge beside every
  bell, so which rings which is readable at a glance.
* Tap any time to edit it — and its number of bells; toggle bells on or off;
  delete with one tap.
* Four bell sounds to choose from — singing bell, Tibetan E flat bowl, gong
  bowl and Satipanya — all matched to the same loudness, so switching changes
  the timbre and never the volume. One bell and three bells are matched too.
* Bell volume and talk volume are set separately, because a spoken recording
  normally has to be much louder than a bowl strike to fill the same room.
  Each has its own Test button that plays at the exact level the room will
  hear. Test bell rings once, which is all it takes to judge the level, and
  Test talk uses the talk that is actually coming up next.

Dharma talk library:

* Add talks from this phone, an Infomaniak kDrive public share link, or a
  podcast RSS feed — every import is downloaded into the app so playback works
  with no network at all.
* Play a talk instantly, or schedule one to play at a set time exactly like a
  bell.
* A player bar with a draggable progress bar — talks often open with minutes
  of silence, so drag straight to the speech instead of waiting it out.
  Restart, 10 seconds back and forward, pause, and both elapsed and remaining
  time, from the app or the notification.
* Optional "keep Bluetooth speaker awake": portable speakers disconnect after
  a few minutes of silence, so the next bell would come faintly from the
  tablet. Turn it on when using an external speaker and it plays a
  barely-audible sound between bells to hold the link open. The bells are
  untouched — still the exact-alarm system, this is only a separate faint
  stream.

No ads, no tracking, no accounts. The schedule repeats every day.

summary.en-US: Rings a bell every so many minutes, until you stop it

description.en-US:
Retreat Walk rings a singing bowl at a fixed interval — every 10 minutes, say —
over and over until you stop it. For switching partners in a paired meditation
exercise, and for sitting with a regular reminder to stay awake.

One number and one button. That is the whole app.

* Set the minutes between bells and press Start. The bell rings at that many
  minutes, then at twice, then three times, and on and on.
* Press Stop in the app, or on the notification, and the session ends.
* The screen shows a countdown to the next bell and how many have rung.

It rings on time:

* Every bell is an exact alarm, the same mechanism the phone's own Clock app
  uses, so it fires even when the device is locked, asleep or in power-saving
  Doze.
* The session runs in a foreground service holding a wake lock, so the system
  cannot mute the bowl or kill it partway through.
* Bells are timed from the start of the session rather than from the previous
  bell, so an hour in they have not drifted away from the clock.
* The notification is silent and carries a Stop action — the bowl is the only
  sound the app ever makes, which is what a quiet room needs.

The bell is a single strike of the Satipanya bowl, shared with Retreat Timer.

No ads, no tracking, no accounts, and no network permission at all.
